In a widely expected move, Volkswagen announced Monday that it will replace the recently retired ID.4 crossover with the upcoming ID.Tiguan. The decision is an acknowledgment by the German automaker that its more recognizable nameplates like Tiguan are likely an easier sell with consumers, especially when it comes to EVs. When it lands in Europe in early 2027, the ID. Tiguan will join the ID.Polo and ID.Cross to round out Volkswagen’s new-and-improved electric lineup. VW also confirmed that the ID.Tiguan will come to the US, where the ID.4 was previously manufactured, “at a later date.” Design details remain under wraps, as the ID.Tiguan is being kept under camouflage for now. First introduced in 2020 , the ID.4 was intended to be VW’s push into mass-market EVs. But rather than go up against big sellers like Tesla’s Model Y, the automaker wanted to compete with high volume gas vehicles like the Toyota RAV4 and Honda CR-V. While it never fully dethroned those rivals, the ID.4 did have some success, selling 950,000 units since 2021. VW says it ranks “among the most successful battery-electric vehicle model series of Volkswagen AG.” VW ended production of the ID.4 at its Chattanooga factory in April 2026. The electric Tiguan will retain much of what worked about the ID.4, while correcting some of its shortcomings, such as its frustrating lack of physical controls . VW plans on giving the ID.Tiguan the same interior look as its ID.3 NEO and ID.Polo, the latter of which is a surprise sales hit in the EU. That means we can expect buttons for all four windows, rather than just two, as well as physical controls for both the volume and climate settings. VW’s Android Automotive-based operating system will also be featured — which means we’ll probably see a Gemini-powered voice assistant. Volkswagen didn’t say whether the ID.Tiguan will get the new Rivian-developed software and zonal architecture that is expected to make its debut on the low-cost ID.Every1 hatchback . Total online spend in the U.S. will top $275 billion, according to Adobe, but many will use the season to stock up on necessities. U.S. online sales for the 2026 holiday season, which runs between Nov. 1 and Dec. 31, are expected to grow 6.7% year over year to $275.1 billion, according to the latest data from Adobe. For Cyber Week, which is the five-day period between Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday, online sales are expected to be up 7.4% year over year to $47.5 billion, with Cyber Monday projected to set a new U.S. e-commerce record and bring in more than $15 billion online in a single day, representing a 6.2% year-over-year uptick. Black Friday spending is growing more quickly than Cyber Monday, and is expected to be up 9.2% to $12.9 billion, representing the second-biggest single day of U.S. holiday spend. It will be buoyed by hefty discounts on big-ticket items including televisions and appliances, as well as apparel sales. Traditionally, consumers have used holiday discounts to buy gifts, Adobe said. However, this year shoppers will be more likely to stock up on essentials as economic concerns push U.S. consumers to focus on value . For Cyber Week, Adobe projected that online sales of personal hygiene products would grow 150% compared to average September 2026 sales levels, with clothing basics expected to be up by 210%. In addition, baby product sales will grow 113%, pet products will be up 93% and household cleaning sales will increase 49%. That said, the overall main categories for shoppers this holiday season are expected to be electronics ($63.3 billion, up 5.9% year over year) and apparel ($51.3 billion, up 4.7% year over year). Online furniture sales are projected to grow 7.3% to $33.4 billion, while grocery, toys and cosmetics are projected to grow about 10% each year over year to $26.1 billion, $9.6 billion and $9.2 billion, respectively. Average discounts are expected to be similar to 2025 levels across all categories. Ahead of the holidays, October’s Prime Big Deal Days is shaping up to be a major pre-season shopping event. The two-day happening is forecast to bring in almost $10 billion online, and “has become an industrywide e-commerce moment, with discounts happening broadly across U.S. retailers,” per Adobe. Overall October online sales are projected to increase 8% year over year to $95.8 billion. “[Prime Big Deal Days in October] has changed the shape of the holiday season, pushing U.S. retailers to manage promotions and inventory effectively to capture an additional pre-season spike in shopping interest,” Adobe said in its report. Meanwhile, Thanksgiving Day sales are expected to be up 8.5% year over year to $6.9 billion, with a record 63% of online spending coming from mobile devices. That’s up from 61.6% in 2025, and also outpaces the overall projected mobile spend for the season (57.4%). Adobe attributed the increase in mobile purchasing to an uptick in impulse shopping. Mobile spending is also driving online buy now, pay later financing, with 82% of BNPL spending coming through mobile versus desktop. Adobe said impulse shopping has also driven the adoption of this flexible financing method, and overall BNPL spend is projected to increase 6.6% year over year to $21.3 billion this holiday season. The biggest day for BNPL spending will be Cyber Monday, which is projected to hit $1.09 billion in online BNPL spending. This will be the second straight year BNPL has driven more than a billion dollars in sales for Cyber Monday. Artificial intelligence will also play a major part in consumers’ discovery journey, with Adobe projecting that AI traffic to U.S. online retail sites this holiday season will increase 130% year over year. Adobe cited a recent survey that found that 77% of respondents who used AI for online shopping said they felt “more confident in their purchase,” with another 69% reporting that they were less likely to return something they bought.

For Cyber Week, Adobe projected that online sales of personal hygiene products would grow 150% compared to average September 2026 sales levels, with clothing basics expected to be up by 210%. In addition, baby product sales will grow 113%, pet products will be up 93% and household cleaning sales will increase 49%.

That said, the overall main categories for shoppers this holiday season are expected to be electronics ($63.3 billion, up 5.9% year over year) and apparel ($51.3 billion, up 4.7% year over year). Online furniture sales are projected to grow 7.3% to $33.4 billion, while grocery, toys and cosmetics are projected to grow about 10% each year over year to $26.1 billion, $9.6 billion and $9.2 billion, respectively.
Average discounts are expected to be similar to 2025 levels across all categories.

Ahead of the holidays, October’s Prime Big Deal Days is shaping up to be a major pre-season shopping event. The two-day happening is forecast to bring in almost $10 billion online, and “has become an industrywide e-commerce moment, with discounts happening broadly across U.S. retailers,” per Adobe. Overall October online sales are projected to increase 8% year over year to $95.8 billion.

“[Prime Big Deal Days in October] has changed the shape of the holiday season, pushing U.S. retailers to manage promotions and inventory effectively to capture an additional pre-season spike in shopping interest,” Adobe said in its report.

Meanwhile, Thanksgiving Day sales are expected to be up 8.5% year over year to $6.9 billion, with a record 63% of online spending coming from mobile devices. That’s up from 61.6% in 2025, and also outpaces the overall projected mobile spend for the season (57.4%). Adobe attributed the increase in mobile purchasing to an uptick in impulse shopping.

Mobile spending is also driving online buy now, pay later financing, with 82% of BNPL spending coming through mobile versus desktop. Adobe said impulse shopping has also driven the adoption of this flexible financing method, and overall BNPL spend is projected to increase 6.6% year over year to $21.3 billion this holiday season. The biggest day for BNPL spending will be Cyber Monday, which is projected to hit $1.09 billion in online BNPL spending. This will be the second straight year BNPL has driven more than a billion dollars in sales for Cyber Monday.

Artificial intelligence will also play a major part in consumers’ discovery journey, with Adobe projecting that AI traffic to U.S. online retail sites this holiday season will increase 130% year over year.

Adobe cited a recent survey that found that 77% of respondents who used AI for online shopping said they felt “more confident in their purchase,” with another 69% reporting that they were less likely to return something they bought.

For years, the AKU ASA Volunteer Camp has served as a meeting ground where architecture students and local craftsmen exchange skills that are otherwise fading from one generation to the next. Song Phi Nong Primary School needed a small sanitary facility, and its site offered little more than open ground shaded by a mature Nontri tree. The volunteers arrived with almost no construction experience and eleven days to close that gap. Instead of repeating the pavilions and multipurpose halls that had defined previous editions of the camp, AKU ASA 20 asked a different question: what remains to learn when the same building type is designed every year? Choosing a toilet as the year’s project shifted the focus from structure and space toward a discipline rarely addressed in student work: sanitary design, and how plumbing systems are shaped by both the building and its site. Shade, airflow, and reclaimed wood shape school toilet’s design The layout responds directly to context: the shade cast by the Nontri tree and the site’s natural airflow transform the in-between space linking the sinks and the toilet stalls into an area that can double as a place to cool off, rest, or play, rather than a purely functional corridor. Materials carried their own history into the project. The design team , led by SEP studio, sourced reclaimed wood from the school’s original building, a Chinese-style classroom constructed roughly sixty years earlier, giving the new structure a physical link to the school’s own past. Every component was built by hand by the volunteers. The result is a modest building, but one that reframes what a student volunteer camp can teach: that architecture education extends beyond form-making into infrastructure, material reuse, and the patient transfer of craft knowledge from one generation to the next. name: Phi Sorn Nong Toilet location: Suphanburi Province, Thailand designboom has received this project from our DIY submissions feature, where we welcome our readers to submit their own work for publication. items.articleText: It’s been a while since we’ve seen a big price cut on a capable robot vacuum and mop hybrid that can scale over short steps and threshold to hunt messes. Dreame’s X50 Ultra is the model that my colleague Jen recommends for hard floors and carpets, and it’s down to $899.99 at Amazon for Prime members (originally $1,599.99, but commonly around $1,100). It’s actually a bit cheaper ($849.99) directly through Dreame’s site if you have a free account there. $1099.99 $899.99 at Amazon (for Prime members) $1099.99 $849.99 at Dreame (with free account) The X50 Ultra debuted in early 2025, and still made the cut for Jen’s 2026 list of the best robot vacuums , thanks to its huge list of features that are executed well, for the most part. It’s a great vacuum and mop, and its mopping pads extend out, sweeping underneath cabinets and other furniture that sits close to the floor. Also of note is its ability to climb over thresholds up to 6 centimeters (over 2 inches) tall, ensuring it won’t get stuck where other vacuums may stumble. Like any good robot vacuum and mop, there isn’t much you’ll have to do to maintain on a day-to-day basis. It can remove, wash, and dry its mops autonomously, and its self-emptying bin can collect debris it sucks up for several weeks. Dreame claims you won’t have to empty it for 100 days, but that obviously depends on how messy your place is. Also, you’ll likely have to refill its water tank frequently if you’re mopping a lot. Other fantastic Verge-approved deals Woot has a pretty good deal happening on “Grade A” condition refurbished units of Asus’ ROG Ally with the AMD Ryzen Z1 Extreme processor (16GB RAM, 512GB SSD) and a 90-day warranty. Priced at $529.99, the offer code CHEERS knocks 20 percent off that total for the rest of the day (September 28th). New customers who use the code get 30 percent off. For 20 percent off, that’s about $425, or $371 with the 30-percent discount. This model is a solid competitor to the Steam Deck LCD, with a higher-res 1080p screen with a 120Hz refresh rate. Its Z1 Extreme processor is faster, too, so this might be the deal you’ve been looking for if you’re striking out on handheld deals. Read our 2023 review. Another deal that jumped out from Woot is for the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro wireless headset for the PlayStation, PC, and Switch. The white version in new condition is about $192 with the code CHEERS , or down to around $168 if you happen to be a new Woot customer who uses the code. Its current $239.99 price is already good enough to earn it a spot in this roundup, but the current discount brings it down to “best-ever” territory. And while digital sales are on the rise, offline sales still account for around three-quarters of overall retail sales, according to research last year from EY . But successful store experiences push beyond a transaction. They foster connection with customers and encourage discovery of new products. Over the past year, retailers from all sectors have announced partnerships and new formats — from dollar stores shrinking their stores , to Amazon multiplying its square footage . Below, we revisit five store concepts that debuted in 2026. 1. Target Beauty Studio The Target Beauty Studio concept at a store in Ellicott City, Maryland, on Sept. 26, 2026. Caroline Jansen/Retail Dive After teasing plans in March, Target officially opened its Beauty Studio concept in about 600 stores earlier this month. The concept replaced the Ulta Beauty shop-in-shops that closed when the partnership between Target and the beauty retailer ended in August . The new space features over 1,600 products from 90 brands — two-thirds of which are new to the mass merchant and include Dyson, Sunday Riley and Boy Smells. The Target Beauty Studio spaces will also be staffed by dedicated beauty advisers to offer product recommendations and guidance. The concept will feature minis of certain items, product testing on select SKUs and a rotating assortment of curated products such as “Editors’ Picks” and “Standouts of the Season.” "It's an inspiring destination to discover what's new, now and next in beauty — and a powerful example of how our merchandising authority comes to life through an elevated guest experience,” Amanda Nusz, senior vice president of merchandising, essentials and beauty at Target, said in a statement. 2. The Crenshaw Rec by Foot Locker Permission granted by Foot Locker Foot Locker and Nike teamed up this summer to introduce a new concept, The Crenshaw Rec . The concept aims to provide a hyperlocal space, taking inspiration from neighborhood recreation centers. To that end, the concept features an equipment room, open gym, creative workspaces and a resource center that will host programming. Alongside Nike, the concept was developed with Crenshaw High School, Nipsey Hussle’s The Marathon Brand, Los Angeles designer Gavin Mathieu and local vendors. "The Crenshaw Rec by Foot Locker reflects our commitment to investing in the communities that have shaped our brand and continue to move sneaker culture forward," Brett O'Brien, Foot Locker’s chief marketing officer, said in a statement. "Together with Nike, Inc. and respected voices across Crenshaw, we're proud to create a destination that honors the neighborhood's rich legacy while inspiring the next generation through sport, culture, and community." The Crenshaw concept debuted as Nike began quietly closing some of its local neighborhood stores, originally dubbed Nike Live, across the country. The stores, which were rebranded to Nike Well Collective in 2023, were shuttered in several states including California, Maryland, Illinois, Florida and Colorado. The co-created concept from Foot Locker and Nike also comes as both retailers embark on turnarounds. Foot Locker, now under the ownership of Dick’s Sporting Goods, has been working to refresh hundreds of its stores, including reducing the number of SKUs on display and creating better presentation overall. And Nike, under the direction of Elliott Hill , has been making some progress in its turnaround , though analysts have said the retailer is “not yet out of the woods.” 3. As of August, the new format is featured in three of the retailer’s stores — Easton, Ohio; Irving, Texas; and Rogers, Arkansas — and the company plans to eventually roll out elements of the concept to all stores. "The new format reflects our customers' desire for more inspiration and hands-on, analog experiences, while providing a space for the local community to connect, create, and celebrate,” CEO David Boone said in a statement. In the new concept, Michaels segments the store by different “shopping worlds”: Knit & Sew Shop, Fine Arts, Floral & Greenery, Crafting & Kids, The Party Shop at Michaels, Framing & Personalization Services, Signature Moments, Seasonal & Trends and the Welcome Center. The concept advances Michaels’ efforts to expand its offerings and take share following the bankruptcies of Joann and Party City . 4. Through the shop-in-shops, Best Buy and Meta are “reimagining how consumers shop the next generation of personal technology,” Christa Wittenberg, vice president of global retail sales at Meta, said in a statement. “These are immersive, hands-on spaces built for real discovery — where people can experience firsthand just how stylish, fun, and personal AI glasses and VR really are. We want customers to walk in curious and leave genuinely excited about what's possible." The spaces will be staffed by dedicated Meta sales specialists to educate shoppers on the products and capabilities. Customers are able to try on various AI glasses, experience immersive demos and interact with built-in prompts intended to show how the products can be used in everyday life. The tie-up with Meta is part of a broader footprint shift from Best Buy that emphasizes more medium- and small-format locations. The concept also follows a partnership the retailer launched last year with Ikea to open shop-in-shops within its stores. The partnership has since expanded to offer Best Buy consultation spaces at select Ikea stores. 5. "Our athletes are increasingly looking for new ways to rep their favorite teams, their style and the latest trends," David Progar, senior vice president of Licensed at Dick's, said in a statement. "By partnering with Lids, a leader in licensed headwear, we'll be able to offer them more choices to meet their needs for sport, lifestyle and fandom." In June, Dick’s debuted the Lids concept to nearly 50 of its stores and said at the time that it planned to expand the concept to over 100 locations by the end of the summer. The concepts feature licensed and lifestyle headwear from Lids, and the two retailers worked together on associate training and visual merchandising. The concept adds to other initiatives Dick’s has rolled out related to its physical footprint. Over the summer, the sporting goods retailer opened a pop-up in the Hamptons , highlighting four of its private labels. It has also been expanding its House of Sport and Field House concepts, which have performed well for the retailer .

TechCrunch Desktop Logo TechCrunch Mobile Logo Media & Entertainment More from TechCrunch TechCrunch Brand Studio Image Credits: Kevin Carter FBI reportedly declares ‘cyber security incident’ after hackers steal agents’ personal data 7:50 AM PDT · September 28, 2026 The Federal Bureau of Investigation has reportedly told its agents and support staff that their personal information was stolen in a recent cyberattack that targeted the bureau’s job application portal. It’s the bureau’s first acknowledgement that the personal information of FBI agents was taken in the breach. The FBI has not publicly confirmed a breach beyond a statement last week, in which it said it was aware that a hacking group had claimed a cyberattack, but that the theft of data was “still undetermined.” As reported by MS NOW reporter Ken Dilanian over the weekend, the FBI has since declared a “cyber security incident” in an internal notification to staff, telling employees that their names, addresses, job titles, and their Social Security numbers were exposed. New: The FBI told employees in an internal notification that it has declared a “cyber security incident” related to the hack of the https://t.co/l4iJxC0jA2 portal. Personally identifiable information of FBI employees, including social security numbers, addresses and job titles,… — Ken Dilanian (@KDilanianMSNOW) September 26, 2026 Several media outlets have since confirmed that some of the stolen data included medical information, such as records relating to blood and urine samples , as well as psychiatric reports . The hacking group called ShinyHunters previously told TechCrunch that they “have data on mostly all of FBI,” and a “substantial” amount of information on applicants who applied through the FBIJobs.gov portal. The hackers broke in by exploiting a vulnerability in an Oracle PeopleSoft server, which hosts reams of human resources information on agents and now-employees who applied through the portal. The hackers told TechCrunch that they are not seeking a financial ransom, but are demanding the correction of an earlier FBI-issued report, which they say misrepresents their activities. Justin Sherman, a national security expert, called the data breach a “counterintelligence disaster” for the U.S. government in a blog post for Lawfare . He warned that the data theft would “expose thousands of FBI personnel to profiling, phishing, foreign intelligence approaches, and much more.” While the bureau has notified employees, it’s less clear if the FBI has disclosed the incident to lawmakers in Congress who have oversight of the FBI. Under federal law , alerting Congress is required when an intrusion meets the bar of a “major incident” — such as if a data breach involves the theft of personally identifiable information that is “likely to result in demonstrable harm” to U.S. national security. It’s likely that bureau lawyers are trying to figure that out right now. If a disclosure is required, it would be the FBI’s second known notification to lawmakers this year about a data breach, after hackers, suspected to be Chinese, broke into a surveillance system that exposed targets of FBI surveillance and investigations earlier this year. A spokesperson for the FBI did not respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment on Monday, and a White House spokesperson also did not respond to an email asking if the bureau had declared a major incident. Representatives for several lawmakers whose jurisdictions cover oversight of the FBI did not have any immediate answers. ABC News reports that the FBI’s job site has been the primary way to apply for a job with the bureau since 2017. The portal remains down at the time of publication. FBI reportedly declares ‘cyber security incident’ after hackers steal agents’ personal data
7:50 AM PDT · September 28, 2026

The Federal Bureau of Investigation has reportedly told its agents and support staff that their personal information was stolen in a recent cyberattack that targeted the bureau’s job application portal.

It’s the bureau’s first acknowledgement that the personal information of FBI agents was taken in the breach. The FBI has not publicly confirmed a breach beyond a statement last week, in which it said it was aware that a hacking group had claimed a cyberattack, but that the theft of data was “still undetermined.”

As reported by MS NOW reporter Ken Dilanian over the weekend, the FBI has since declared a “cyber security incident” in an internal notification to staff, telling employees that their names, addresses, job titles, and their Social Security numbers were exposed.

New: The FBI told employees in an internal notification that it has declared a “cyber security incident” related to the hack of the https://t.co/l4iJxC0jA2 portal. Personally identifiable information of FBI employees, including social security numbers, addresses and job titles,…
— Ken Dilanian (@KDilanianMSNOW) September 26, 2026
Several media outlets have since confirmed that some of the stolen data included medical information, such as records relating to blood and urine samples , as well as psychiatric reports .

The hacking group called ShinyHunters previously told TechCrunch that they “have data on mostly all of FBI,” and a “substantial” amount of information on applicants who applied through the FBIJobs.gov portal. The hackers broke in by exploiting a vulnerability in an Oracle PeopleSoft server, which hosts reams of human resources information on agents and now-employees who applied through the portal.
The hackers told TechCrunch that they are not seeking a financial ransom, but are demanding the correction of an earlier FBI-issued report, which they say misrepresents their activities.

Justin Sherman, a national security expert, called the data breach a “counterintelligence disaster” for the U.S. government in a blog post for Lawfare . He warned that the data theft would “expose thousands of FBI personnel to profiling, phishing, foreign intelligence approaches, and much more.”

While the bureau has notified employees, it’s less clear if the FBI has disclosed the incident to lawmakers in Congress who have oversight of the FBI. Under federal law , alerting Congress is required when an intrusion meets the bar of a “major incident” — such as if a data breach involves the theft of personally identifiable information that is “likely to result in demonstrable harm” to U.S. national security.

It’s likely that bureau lawyers are trying to figure that out right now. If a disclosure is required, it would be the FBI’s second known notification to lawmakers this year about a data breach, after hackers, suspected to be Chinese, broke into a surveillance system that exposed targets of FBI surveillance and investigations earlier this year.

A spokesperson for the FBI did not respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment on Monday, and a White House spokesperson also did not respond to an email asking if the bureau had declared a major incident.
Representatives for several lawmakers whose jurisdictions cover oversight of the FBI did not have any immediate answers.
ABC News reports that the FBI’s job site has been the primary way to apply for a job with the bureau since 2017. The portal remains down at the time of publication.

See All by Andrew Liszewski is a senior reporter who’s been covering and reviewing the latest gadgets and tech since 2006, but has loved all things electronic since he was a kid. Everything old is new again as today Bose announced its first pair of wired earbuds since discontinuing the option in 2015. The new tethered earbuds, which are simply called the Bose Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds , do away with battery anxiety and the need to remember to charge them every few days. Their functionality is limited, but they do take advantage of the past 11 years of earbud innovation with the addition of active noise canceling. The earbuds are available for preorder today through Bose’s online store for $99 in three color options: black, white smoke, and a “limited edition” green shade called dewdrop mint. While a release from the company says they’re expected to start shipping on October 15th, Bose’s online store says October 13th. The earbuds’ inline remote can be used to control volume, playback, and cycle through ANC modes. Two microphones on each earbud work alongside Bose’s QuietControl technology to deliver active noise canceling with multiple modes that can be cycled using a button on the headphone’s inline remote. Quiet Mode reduces the intensity of sounds around you while Aware Mode instead boosts them, but you can also turn off ANC entirely. There’s an additional microphone on the inline remote for making phone calls and it’s designed to effectively pick up your voice without having to be held close to your mouth. Instead of a headphone connector on the end of the earbuds’ 4.2-foot cable you’ll find USB-C for connecting to smartphones and laptops with support for lossless audio with minimal latency. The earbuds also come with an IPX4 rating for water resistance so they can survive sweat, rain, and splashes but a complete dunking is a no-no. A zippered carrying case is included along with three sizes of silicone eartips and two sizes of stability wings that can provide a more secure fit during physical activities. TechCrunch Desktop Logo TechCrunch Mobile Logo Media & Entertainment More from TechCrunch TechCrunch Brand Studio Image Credits: Modulate Modulate raises $25M for its voice models and analysis suite 7:05 AM PDT · September 28, 2026 Boston-based voice intelligence startup Modulate has raised $25 in new funding for its platform that uses an array of small models to offer enterprises transcription, emotional analysis, deepfake and AI music detection, and policy enforcement for voice agents in regulated industries. The funding follows a popular trend among investors in the growing voice AI industry: backing companies that are trying to make AI voices sound more human. It also rivals other companies trying to detect the intent behind human conversation by analyzing it, and those trying to protect people and companies from deepfake calls, as it is now easy to clone voices. Modulate’s new funding was led by Future Ventures with participation from Hyperplane and Lakestar. Data from PitchBook indicated that the startup had raised $41 million in funding at a $170 million valuation prior to this round. The startup was founded in 2017 by Mike Pappas and Carter Huffman, who met as MIT physics undergrads. In its early days, the company focused on providing voice modulation for gaming. But later, it started to concentrate on a voice-based moderation tool .
